conviction_note: Q3 (to 30 Sep) will look strong because group AUM recovered to about the Q4-2025 level of ~$7.4bn after BTC rose ~43% in the quarter, and the $40m buyback (~9% of market cap, ~27% of free float) sits under a stock at 0.97x book near its 52-week low. Against that, BTC is ~24% below its quarter-end level, so Q4-to-date AUM and the marks are visibly worse, and the market can see all of this in the crypto tape. The findings sum to +1.4 and the scaled number is +0.36 (p_up 53 x abs 6.0). The gap is deliberate: the backward-looking beat is mostly priced, the bar is disputed, and the day's BTC move will likely dominate.

findings.finding: Q3 asset base recovered sharply. CoinShares' own 27 Oct 6-K says Q3-2026 AUM was 'in line with the 25Q4 level', i.e. about $7.4bn at 30 Sep, against $5.52bn at 30 Jun (+~34%). BTC rose ~43% in Q3 and ETH more. Q3 asset-management fees (H1: $40.0M, ~$20M a quarter) should therefore rise to roughly $21-23M, and the H1 marks should reverse: the treasury loss of $15.4M and the XBT pricing-differential loss of $16.6M (the CFO said the treasury loss was 'largely reversed by Aug 31'). The likely result is a GAAP profit well above the $0.13-0.15 EPS consensus, which is itself disputed. Two caveats: the CFO warned not to read the 31 Aug AUM as the whole quarter, and the gains sit below operating income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the last confirmed results day (H1, 2026-09-14) a revenue decline and net loss drew -3.54%; FY2025 results (2026-05-01) drew +7.27%. No clean read on a beat exists; this name has two confirmed prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the AUM statement and BTC's Q3 move are public. If the market expected a strong Q3 profit, it is not showing in a stock 1.35% above its 52-week low at 0.97x book. With two analysts and a consensus that does not reconcile (FY -$0.01 vs Q3 +$0.13), the headline GAAP EPS could print far above the screen number. A profitable Q3 is not reflected in a P/B below 1.
findings.independence: BTC +42.9% in Q3 (https://cryptobriefing.com/bitcoin-jumps-q3-2026-outperforms-gold-stocks/, 2026-10-02). Peer Galaxy swung to a $323M Q3 profit on the same tape (filed separately). The H1 call figures share the CFO's Sep-14 commentary with the fee-mix finding.

findings.finding: Q4-to-date is visibly weaker. BTC was $63,695 on 17 Nov against ~$84k at 30 Sep (-24%), after six straight weekly declines on Fed-hike repricing and a 5.13% 10-year yield. CoinShares' AUM, which is mostly crypto-price beta (net flows were only ~$74M from June to August), is therefore likely back near ~$5.5-6bn. Q4 will carry negative treasury and XBT-differential marks. Management's quarter-to-date commentary on the call and the October AUM tracker point to a weaker Q4 than Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the H1 call (2026-09-14) management cited post-period AUM recovery and the stock still fell 3.54%. No other forward-commentary reaction is on record.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock is -14.56% over 20 days and -9.52% over 5 days, tracking BTC. The unpriced part is the size of the Q4 mark-to-market losses and any outflows management discloses, which the October AUM tracker (behind an email gate) may already show to subscribers. If fully priced, the stock would not sit at 0.97x a book value that is itself shrinking with crypto prices.
findings.independence: Company says AUM is mostly market-driven (H1 release: AUM fell from $7.40bn to $5.52bn on $27.6M of net inflows; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002087587/000121390026099448/ea030468001ex99-1.htm). This is a proxy: no company Q4 number was found.

findings.finding: Capital return. On 27 Oct the board approved a buyback of up to $40M, about 9% of the $447M market cap and about 27% of the 44.6M-share free float. It is funded by selling the whole corporate ETH treasury and half of the SOL holding in October, before the November crypto drop, and is described as reflecting 'confidence in the Company's earnings potential'. Repurchases were likely blacked out ahead of results and can resume in the window. The call may give the first execution figures.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback announcement day (2026-10-27 bmo) drew +9.76% (baseline row; +5.3% pre-open per https://www.tradingpedia.com/2026/10/27/coinshares-jumps-premarket-on-40m-buyback-plan/). Since then the stock has given that back and more.
findings.why_not_priced: Announced, so the authority is priced. Execution is not: with ~$1.1M a day of turnover, the 10b-18 volume cap (~25% of ADTV) limits buying to ~$0.28M a day, so a disclosed pace or a 10b5-1 plan is new information. Book value per share ($3.44) above spot gives the repurchase an accretive arithmetic the stock does not yet reflect.
findings.independence: Book value $453.21M ($3.44/share), P/B 0.97 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/cshr/statistics). Same 6-K as the Q3 AUM statement, a different fact.

findings.finding: Expectations are low going in. Spot is $3.375, 1.35% above the 52-week low and 60.8% below the high, -9.52% over 5 days and -14.56% over 20. That is 0.97x reported book and ~37% of the $9.00 mean target. On the last results day (H1, 14 Sep) the stock fell 3.54% on a reported loss. The slide tracks BTC, not company news, so a clean Q3 and a steady call face a low bar.
findings.why_not_priced: A stock at book with an active buyback and a profitable quarter in hand is priced for continued crypto weakness. If the market expected the Q3 recovery to carry into book value, the shares would not trade below the $3.44 book per share.

findings.finding: Peer Galaxy Digital reported Q3 2026 on 27 Oct: net income swung to $323M from an $85M Q2 loss, asset-management net inflows exceeded $160M, and AUM plus assets under stake rose 46% QoQ to $10.4bn. The shares reportedly rose. This confirms that a crypto asset manager's Q3 mark-to-market and AUM recovered in the same tape.
findings.link: Both are listed crypto asset managers and stakers marked to the same BTC/ETH/SOL prices. Galaxy's asset-management segment is a small part of its revenue (trading and data centers dominate), so the read-through is partial.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for three weeks, so mostly priced. It mainly corroborates the Q3 recovery.

findings.finding: Fee mix improved into Q3. High-fee products rose from 37% to 43% of AUM between June and August. High-fee products earn about 255-284 bps against 22-27 bps for access products, and the blended yield was 128 bps in H1 (156 bps in 2025, 163 bps at constant mix). Q3 blended fee yield should therefore rise QoQ. The offset is the February cut of the flagship physical BTC ETP fee from 25 to 15 bps.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fee compression was the bear point on H1 (stock -3.54% on 2026-09-14).
findings.why_not_priced: It is in a transcript, not the headline numbers, so a two-analyst screen consensus is unlikely to carry it. If priced, the Q3 revenue consensus ($31.5M) would not sit near H1's quarterly run-rate on AUM that is ~20% higher.
findings.independence: Fee cut and mix detail: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/coinshares-cshr-attracts-inflows-revenue-213505209.html (2026-09-17). Shares the Sep-14 call with the Q3 recovery finding.

findings.finding: Cost base and new businesses. H1 adjusted opex was $20.7M, excluding $4.9M of listing and transition costs that should not recur. Management said underperforming product lines will close in H2. Bastion (active alternative strategies) completed on 2 Sep 2026 and adds costs and revenue from Q3. Q3 is clean of the listing costs, but Bastion's cost is a new item.
findings.why_not_priced: The non-recurrence of listing costs is arithmetic a two-analyst consensus may or may not hold. If it were priced, the FY EPS consensus of -$0.01 would not imply so little H2 profit.

findings.finding: Macro tape into the print is negative. Hot inflation data made a December Fed hike 'all but assured', the 10-year sits at 5.13%, BTC is in its sixth weekly decline, and Fear & Greed read 13 on 14 Nov. This stock's single-day return over the window is dominated by crypto beta (20-day realised vol 67.7%).
findings.why_not_priced: Momentum, not information. It is filed small as a proxy, since nothing says BTC's direction over the window is predictable.

findings.finding: Mid-quarter corporate statements since the 14 Sep call: Matt Morris succeeded Richard Nash as CFO (1 Oct 6-K; the Q3 call is his first); a stablecoin yield product on Safe launched (14 Oct). Neither carries a number that bears on the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced; filed for completeness. A new CFO's first call raises the chance of a reset in presentation or cost framing.

Index demand on a 44.6M-share float would land at that rebalance, not in this window. The announcement itself was public before the print, and the stock fell afterwards.

baseline_tension: The evidence mostly agrees with the baseline: the run-up is negative and tracks BTC's fall, and with no option skew there is no priced direction to cut against. The positive findings (Q3 recovery, buyback, low bar) lean against the run-up only modestly, so p_up sits at 53, not higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar from two disagreeing sources, $0.13/$31.47M vs $0.15/$40.5M, FY not reconciling): Q3 recovery finding capped from +1.0 to +0.7
Rule 2 (one-offs): noted that much of the Q3 beat is treasury and XBT-differential marks below operating income; already reflected in the capped +0.7, not cut twice

Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a proxy): macro finding trimmed from -0.5 to -0.4; the Q4-to-date finding kept at -1.0 because AUM is mechanically crypto-priced per the company's own H1 release
Untrustworthy reaction history: rebuilt the base rate from the two confirmed releases (+7.27% FY25, -3.54% H1-26); abs_move_pct 6.0 left unchanged
Rule 7 (short interest checked before negatives): 1.91% of float and 2.99 days to cover is not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk for a squeeze
